+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import pytest
+import regex as re
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import CacheConfig, ModelConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import ColumnParallelLinear
+from vllm.models.hy_v4_flash.nvidia.attention import HYV4FlashMLAAttention
+from vllm.models.hy_v4_flash.nvidia.swa import FlashSWABackend
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.transformers_utils.configs.hy_v4 import HYV4Config
+from vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager import SlidingWindowManager
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import MLAAttentionSpec
+
+NUM_HEADS, NOPE, ROPE, V_DIM, KV_LORA_RANK = 8, 128, 64, 128, 512
+SLIDING_WINDOW = 512
+
+
+def _flash_swa_layer(cache_config: CacheConfig) -> HYV4FlashMLAAttention:
+    kv_b_proj = ColumnParallelLinear(
+        KV_LORA_RANK, NUM_HEADS * (NOPE + V_DIM), bias=False
+    )
+    return HYV4FlashMLAAttention(
+        num_heads=NUM_HEADS,
+        scale=1.0,
+        qk_nope_head_dim=NOPE,
+        qk_rope_head_dim=ROPE,
+        v_head_dim=V_DIM,
+        q_lora_rank=512,
+        kv_lora_rank=KV_LORA_RANK,
+        kv_b_proj=kv_b_proj,
+        cache_config=cache_config,
+        prefix="model.layers.0.self_attn.attn",
+        attn_backend=FlashSWABackend,
+        use_sparse=True,
+        sliding_window=SLIDING_WINDOW,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100),
+    reason="HY V4 Flash sparse MLA runs on SM100",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kv_cache_dtype", ["fp8", "fp8_e4m3", "fp8_ds_mla"])
+def test_flash_swa_layer_serves_fp8_ds_mla(
+    dist_init, workspace_init, tmp_path, kv_cache_dtype: str
+):
+    """HY V4 Flash window layers run the paged fp8_ds_mla cache that base
+    sliding-window MLA rejects, so fp8 aliases must yield a sliding-window
+    fp8_ds_mla KV cache."""
+    hf_config = HYV4Config(
+        hidden_size=256,
+        num_hidden_layers=1,
+        num_attention_heads=NUM_HEADS,
+        num_key_value_heads=NUM_HEADS,
+        q_lora_rank=128,
+        max_position_embeddings=8192,
+        layer_types=["deepseek_sparse_attention"],
+    )
+    hf_config.architectures = ["HYV4ForCausalLM"]
+    hf_config.save_pretrained(tmp_path)
+    vllm_config = VllmConfig(
+        model_config=ModelConfig(
+            model=str(tmp_path), dtype="bfloat16", skip_tokenizer_init=True
+        ),
+        cache_config=CacheConfig(cache_dtype=kv_cache_dtype),
+    )
+    with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config), torch.device("cuda"):
+        layer = _flash_swa_layer(vllm_config.cache_config)
+
+    layer_config = layer.get_kv_cache_config(vllm_config)
+    assert layer_config.manager_cls is SlidingWindowManager
+    assert isinstance(layer_config.spec, MLAAttentionSpec)
+    assert layer_config.spec.cache_dtype_str == "fp8_ds_mla"
+
+
+def test_flash_swa_layer_rejects_nvfp4_ds_mla(dist_init, default_vllm_config):
+    with pytest.raises(
+        ValueError,
+        match=re.escape(
+            "Sliding-window MLA does not support kv_cache_dtype=nvfp4_ds_mla."
+        ),
+    ):
+        _flash_swa_layer(CacheConfig(cache_dtype="nvfp4_ds_mla"))

[Bugfix][Frontend] Refresh echoed text after prompt truncation (#62691)

Signed-off-by: waizuichougou <2082431897@qq.com>
Co-authored-by: OpenAI Codex <noreply@openai.com>

@@ -171,6 +171,15 @@ The following extra parameters are supported:
     --8<-- "vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py:completion-extra-params"
     ```
 
+#### Echo with prompt truncation
+
+`truncate_prompt_tokens` and `truncation_side` are vLLM extensions. In the Python
+Completions API, when `echo=true` and an explicit `truncation_side` causes
+post-tokenization truncation, the echoed text is rebuilt from the retained tokens.
+Tokenizer-added special tokens are omitted from the text and echoed logprobs;
+special tokens supplied in the text are preserved. Model input IDs, prompt-token
+usage and `return_token_ids` responses retain the full truncated token sequence.
+
 ### Chat API
 
 Our Chat API is compatible with [OpenAI's Chat Completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat);

+async def test_truncated_echo_excludes_only_added_special_tokens(
+    client: openai.AsyncOpenAI,
+    prompt: str,
+    keep: int,

+    stream: bool,
+    max_tokens: int,

+    extra_body = {"truncate_prompt_tokens": keep, "truncation_side": "right"}
+    generated = await client.completions.create(
+        model="facebook/opt-125m",
+        prompt=prompt,
+        max_tokens=max(1, max_tokens),

+    )
+    tokenizer = get_tokenizer("facebook/opt-125m")
+    assert generated.choices[0].prompt_token_ids == tokenizer.encode(prompt)[:keep]
+    assert generated.usage is not None
+    assert generated.usage.prompt_tokens == keep
+    response = await client.completions.create(
+        model="facebook/opt-125m",
+        prompt=prompt,
+        echo=True,
+        max_tokens=max_tokens,
+        temperature=0.0,
+        logprobs=0,
+        stream=stream,
+        extra_body=extra_body,
+    )
+    choices = (
+        [chunk.choices[0] async for chunk in response] if stream else response.choices
+    )
+    if not stream:
+        assert response.usage is not None
+        assert response.usage.prompt_tokens == keep
+    text = "".join(choice.text for choice in choices)
+    generated_text = generated.choices[0].text if max_tokens else ""
+    assert text == expected + generated_text
+    offset = 0
+    for choice in choices:
+        assert choice.logprobs is not None
+        assert len(choice.logprobs.tokens) == len(choice.logprobs.token_logprobs)
+        assert len(choice.logprobs.tokens) == len(choice.logprobs.top_logprobs)
+        for token, text_offset in zip(
+            choice.logprobs.tokens, choice.logprobs.text_offset, strict=True
+        ):
+            assert text_offset == offset
+            assert text[text_offset : text_offset + len(token)] == token
+            offset += len(token)
+    assert offset == len(text)
+

 Automatic Prefix Caching (APC in short) caches the KV cache of existing queries, so that a new query can directly reuse the KV cache if it shares the same prefix with one of the existing queries, allowing the new query to skip the computation of the shared part.
 
-!!! note
-    Technical details on how vLLM implements APC can be found [here](../design/prefix_caching.md).
+APC reuses only the longest run of full blocks at the start of the prompt that is already cached. Each block's hash covers every token before it, so a prompt that differs at one token recomputes that block and every block after it, even if the later text is identical. Technical details on how vLLM implements APC can be found [here](../design/prefix_caching.md).
 
 ## Enabling APC in vLLM
 
@@ -87,7 +86,13 @@ With `--prefix-match-unit`, a request can resume inside a Mamba block, so Replay
 We describe two example workloads, where APC can provide huge performance benefit:
 
 - Long document query, where the user repeatedly queries the same long document (e.g. software manual or annual report) with different queries. In this case, instead of processing the long document again and again, APC allows vLLM to process this long document *only once*, and all future requests can avoid recomputing this long document by reusing its KV cache. This allows vLLM to serve future requests with much higher throughput and much lower latency.
-- Multi-round conversation, where the user may chat with the application multiple times in the same chatting session. In this case, instead of processing the whole chatting history again and again, APC allows vLLM to reuse the processing results of the chat history across all future rounds of conversation, allowing vLLM to serve future requests with much higher throughput and much lower latency.
+- Multi-round conversation, where the user may chat with the application multiple times in the same chatting session. In this case, instead of processing the whole chatting history again and again, APC allows vLLM to reuse the processing results of the chat history across all future rounds of conversation, allowing vLLM to serve future requests with much higher throughput and much lower latency. This only works while earlier messages stay token-identical between rounds and new content is appended at the end.
+
+## Measuring the hit rate
+
+Divide the increase in `vllm:prefix_cache_hits` by the increase in `vllm:prefix_cache_queries` (both count tokens).

+
+//! `OffloadingConnector` telemetry: the `vllm:kv_offload_*` families.
+//!
+//! Python declares these families as metadata tables, the connector's own
+//! (`get_connector_metric_definitions`) and each offloading spec's
+//! (`build_metric_definitions`), and keys its stats payload by metric name.
+//! [`DEFINITIONS`] mirrors the tables of the built-in specs, so a family
+//! reviews against its Python definition row by row.
+
+use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, HashMap};
+
+use prometheus_client::metrics::family::{Family, MetricConstructor};
+use prometheus_client::registry::Registry;
+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+
+use crate::{EngineLabels, F64Counter, F64Gauge, Histogram};
+
+/// OffloadingConnector telemetry.
+///
+/// The `types`/`data` envelope of [`SimpleCpuOffloadStats`], plus `info`.
+/// The families depend on the configured offloading spec, so `data` stays
+/// keyed by metric name and each name is resolved against [`DEFINITIONS`];
+/// `types` is not read.
+///
+/// Original Python definition: `OffloadingConnectorStats` in
+/// `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/metrics.py`.
+///
+/// [`SimpleCpuOffloadStats`]: super::SimpleCpuOffloadStats
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct OffloadingStats {
+    /// Samples of one interval, keyed by metric name and then by the
+    /// metric's label values (a Python tuple, empty when unlabeled).
+    pub data: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<Vec<String>, OffloadingSample>>,
+    /// `vllm:kv_offload_config_info` facts, one mapping of label name to
+    /// value per series, with the values already stringified by Python. The
+    /// scheduler sends them once; `None` otherwise.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub info: Option<Vec<BTreeMap<String, String>>>,
+}
+
+/// One OffloadingConnector sample: a counter increment or gauge value, or
+/// the observations of a histogram.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+#[serde(untagged)]
+pub enum OffloadingSample {
+    Value(f64),
+    Observations(Vec<f64>),
+}
+
+const LOAD_BYTES: &str = "vllm:kv_offload_load_bytes";
+const LOAD_TIME: &str = "vllm:kv_offload_load_time";
+const LOAD_SIZE: &str = "vllm:kv_offload_load_size";
+const STORE_BYTES: &str = "vllm:kv_offload_store_bytes";
+const STORE_TIME: &str = "vllm:kv_offload_store_time";
+const STORE_SIZE: &str = "vllm:kv_offload_store_size";
+
+const TRANSFER_SIZE_BUCKETS: &[f64] =
+    &[1e6, 5e6, 10e6, 20e6, 40e6, 60e6, 80e6, 100e6, 150e6, 200e6];
+const LOOKUP_SYNC_DELAY_BUCKETS: &[f64] = &[
+    0.00001, 0.00005, 0.0001, 0.0005, 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0,
+];
+const LOOKUP_ASYNC_DELAY_BUCKETS: &[f64] = &[
+    0.0001, 0.0005, 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 5.0, 10.0,
+];
+const DEFERRED_RELEASE_HOLD_BUCKETS: &[f64] = &[
+    0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 60.0, 120.0,
+];
+const PROMOTION_LATENCY_BUCKETS: &[f64] = &[
+    0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, 30.0, 60.0,
+];
+const CPU_ALLOCATION_SIZE_BUCKETS: &[f64] = &[
+    1.0, 4.0, 16.0, 64.0, 256.0, 1024.0, 4096.0, 16384.0, 65536.0, 262144.0,

+

+/// Constructor of histograms with fixed bucket bounds.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+struct FixedBuckets(&'static [f64]);
+
+impl MetricConstructor<Histogram> for FixedBuckets {
+    fn new_metric(&self) -> Histogram {
+        Histogram::new(self.0.iter().copied())
+    }
+}
+
+/// Label set of these families, whose label names vary by family.
+type Labels = Vec<(String, String)>;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+enum OffloadFamily {
+    Counter(Family<Labels, F64Counter>),
+    Gauge(Family<Labels, F64Gauge>),
+    Histogram(Family<Labels, Histogram, FixedBuckets>),
+}
+
+/// The `vllm:kv_offload_*` families. Mirrors `OffloadPromMetrics`.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+pub(super) struct OffloadingMetrics {
+    families: HashMap<&'static str, (&'static Definition, OffloadFamily)>,
+    // Deprecated predecessors of the flat transfer families, labeled by
+    // `transfer_type`.
+    total_bytes: Family<Labels, F64Counter>,
+    total_time: Family<Labels, F64Counter>,
+    size: Family<Labels, Histogram, FixedBuckets>,
+    config_info: Family<Labels, F64Gauge>,
+}
+
+impl OffloadingMetrics {
+    pub(super) fn register(registry: &mut Registry) -> Self {
+        let families = DEFINITIONS
+            .iter()
+            .map(|definition| {
+                let family = match definition.kind {
+                    Kind::Counter => {
+                        let family = Family::default();
+                        registry.register(definition.name, definition.help, family.clone());
+                        OffloadFamily::Counter(family)
+                    }
+                    Kind::Gauge => {
+                        let family = Family::default();
+                        registry.register(definition.name, definition.help, family.clone());
+                        OffloadFamily::Gauge(family)
+                    }
+                    Kind::Histogram(buckets) => {
+                        let family = Family::new_with_constructor(FixedBuckets(buckets));
+                        registry.register(definition.name, definition.help, family.clone());
+                        OffloadFamily::Histogram(family)
+                    }
+                };
+                (definition.name, (definition, family))
+            })
+            .collect();
+
+        let total_bytes = Family::default();
+        registry.register(
+            "vllm:kv_offload_total_bytes",
+            "Number of bytes offloaded by KV connector",
+            total_bytes.clone(),
+        );
+        let total_time = Family::default();
+        registry.register(
+            "vllm:kv_offload_total_time",
+            "Total time measured by all KV offloading operations",
+            total_time.clone(),
+        );
+        let size = Family::new_with_constructor(FixedBuckets(TRANSFER_SIZE_BUCKETS));
+        registry.register(
+            "vllm:kv_offload_size",
+            "Histogram of KV offload transfer size, in bytes",
+            size.clone(),
+        );
+
+        let config_info = Family::default();
+        registry.register(
+            "vllm:kv_offload_config_info",
+            "Static configuration of the KV offload managers of this engine instance. The \
+             configured offloading spec declares the label names, and each manager fills the \
+             values, so a series appears from the first scheduler step of its engine. A manager \
+             reports one series for each configuration it holds, and a label of its own tells \
+             the series apart. Each engine reports its own configuration, not the instance total",
+            config_info.clone(),
+        );
+
+        Self {
+            families,
+            total_bytes,
+            total_time,
+            size,
+            config_info,
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn record(&self, engine: &EngineLabels, stats: &OffloadingStats) {
+        if let Some(info) = &stats.info {
+            self.record_config_info(engine, info);
+        }
+        for (name, samples) in &stats.data {
+            for (label_values, sample) in samples {
+                self.record_sample(engine, name, label_values, sample);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Record one family's sample. A family Rust does not define, a label
+    /// count other than its definition's, or a sample of the wrong shape is
+    /// dropped; Python asserts on all three.
+    fn record_sample(
+        &self,
+        engine: &EngineLabels,
+        name: &str,
+        label_values: &[String],
+        sample: &OffloadingSample,
+    ) {
+        let Some((definition, family)) = self.families.get(name) else {
+            return;
+        };
+        if label_values.len() != definition.labels.len() {
+            return;
+        }
+        let labels = engine_labels(engine)
+            .chain(
+                definition
+                    .labels
+                    .iter()
+                    .zip(label_values)
+                    .map(|(name, value)| ((*name).to_string(), value.clone())),
+            )
+            .collect();
+        match (family, sample) {
+            (OffloadFamily::Counter(family), OffloadingSample::Value(value)) => {
+                family.get_or_create(&labels).inc_by(*value);
+            }
+            (OffloadFamily::Gauge(family), OffloadingSample::Value(value)) => {
+                family.get_or_create(&labels).set(*value);
+            }
+            (OffloadFamily::Histogram(family), OffloadingSample::Observations(values)) => {
+                let histogram = family.get_or_create(&labels);
+                for value in values {
+                    histogram.observe(*value);
+                }
+            }
+            _ => return,
+        }
+        self.record_deprecated(engine, name, sample);
+    }
+
+    /// Feed the deprecated `transfer_type` families from the flat transfer
+    /// families, as Python does for `CPUOffloadingSpec` and its subclasses,
+    /// which cover every built-in spec.
+    fn record_deprecated(&self, engine: &EngineLabels, name: &str, sample: &OffloadingSample) {
+        let transfer_type = match name {
+            LOAD_BYTES | LOAD_TIME | LOAD_SIZE => "CPU_to_GPU",
+            STORE_BYTES | STORE_TIME | STORE_SIZE => "GPU_to_CPU",
+            _ => return,
+        };
+        let labels = engine_labels(engine)
+            .chain([("transfer_type".to_string(), transfer_type.to_string())])
+            .collect();
+        match (name, sample) {
+            (LOAD_BYTES | STORE_BYTES, OffloadingSample::Value(value)) => {
+                self.total_bytes.get_or_create(&labels).inc_by(*value);
+            }
+            (LOAD_TIME | STORE_TIME, OffloadingSample::Value(value)) => {
+                self.total_time.get_or_create(&labels).inc_by(*value);
+            }
+            (LOAD_SIZE | STORE_SIZE, OffloadingSample::Observations(values)) => {
+                let histogram = self.size.get_or_create(&labels);
+                for value in values {
+                    histogram.observe(*value);
+                }
+            }
+            _ => {}
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Publish one engine's `vllm:kv_offload_config_info` series, one per
+    /// mapping of label name to value, each set to 1.
+    ///
+    /// Python labels every series with the names the offloading spec declares,
+    /// empty where a series fills none. Rust does not know the spec, so it
+    /// takes the names the series fill; the two agree unless a declared name
+    /// is filled by no series, which Python warns about.
+    fn record_config_info(&self, engine: &EngineLabels, series: &[BTreeMap<String, String>]) {
+        let names: BTreeSet<&String> = series.iter().flat_map(BTreeMap::keys).collect();
+        for info in series {
+            let labels = engine_labels(engine)
+                .chain(names.iter().map(|name| {
+                    let value = info.get(*name).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
+                    ((*name).clone(), value)
+                }))
+                .collect();
+            self.config_info.get_or_create(&labels).set(1.0);
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+fn engine_labels(engine: &EngineLabels) -> impl Iterator<Item = (String, String)> {
+    [
+        ("model_name".to_string(), engine.model_name.clone()),
+        ("engine".to_string(), engine.engine.to_string()),
+    ]
+    .into_iter()
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+    use expect_test::expect;
+    use itertools::Itertools as _;
+
+    use super::{OffloadingSample, OffloadingStats};
+    use crate::{KvConnectorStats, Metrics, MultiConnectorStats};
+
+    /// Records `OffloadingConnectorStats` payloads into the `vllm:kv_offload_*`
+    /// families: the flat transfer families also feed their deprecated
+    /// `transfer_type` predecessors, the config facts become
+    /// `vllm:kv_offload_config_info`, and a family Rust does not define or a
+    /// sample with the wrong label count is dropped.
+    #[test]
+    fn offloading_stats_are_recorded_into_kv_offload_metrics() {
+        let metrics = Metrics::new();
+        let handles = metrics.scheduler.resolve_handles("model", 0);
+        // Series of one family render in hash order, so sort them.
+        let kv_offload_series = || {
+            metrics
+                .render()
+                .unwrap()
+                .lines()
+                .filter(|line| line.starts_with("vllm:kv_offload_") && !line.contains("_bucket{"))
+                .sorted()
+                .join("\n")
+        };
+
+        // Like Python, no series before the connector reports.
+        expect![[""]].assert_eq(&kv_offload_series());
+
+        let value = |value| BTreeMap::from([(vec![], OffloadingSample::Value(value))]);
+        let interval = |usage, info| OffloadingStats {
+            data: BTreeMap::from([
+                ("vllm:kv_offload_load_bytes".to_string(), value(4096.0)),
+                ("vllm:kv_offload_store_time".to_string(), value(0.25)),
+                (
+                    "vllm:kv_offload_store_size".to_string(),
+                    BTreeMap::from([(vec![], OffloadingSample::Observations(vec![2e6, 3e6]))]),
+                ),
+                (
+                    "vllm:kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc".to_string(),
+                    value(usage),
+                ),
+                // `TieringOffloadingSpec` families, labeled by tier.
+                (
+                    "vllm:kv_offload_tiering_chunk_hits".to_string(),
+                    BTreeMap::from([(vec!["1:kvcr".to_string()], OffloadingSample::Value(3.0))]),
+                ),
+                (
+                    "vllm:kv_offload_tiering_promotion_latency_seconds".to_string(),
+                    BTreeMap::from([(
+                        vec!["1:kvcr".to_string(), "success".to_string()],
+                        OffloadingSample::Observations(vec![0.02]),
+                    )]),
+                ),
+                // Wrong label count for an unlabeled family.
+                (
+                    "vllm:kv_offload_allocation_failure".to_string(),
+                    BTreeMap::from([(vec!["x".to_string()], OffloadingSample::Value(1.0))]),
+                ),
+                // A family of a spec Rust does not know.
+                ("vllm:kv_offload_custom_spec_total".to_string(), value(1.0)),
+            ]),
+            info,
+        };
+        let info = vec![BTreeMap::from([
+            ("cpu_num_chunks".to_string(), "64".to_string()),
+            ("cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens".to_string(), "None".to_string()),
+        ])];
+        // Once as the only connector, once as a `MultiConnector` child:
+        // counters and histograms add up, gauges keep the latest value.
+        for kv_connector_stats in [
+            KvConnectorStats::Offloading(interval(0.5, Some(info))),
+            KvConnectorStats::Multi(Box::new(MultiConnectorStats {
+                offloading: Some(interval(0.75, None)),
+                ..Default::default()
+            })),
+        ] {
+            handles.kv_connector.record(&kv_connector_stats);
+        }
+
+        expect![[r#"
+            vllm:kv_offload_config_info{model_name="model",engine="0",cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens="None",cpu_num_chunks="64"} 1.0
+            vllm:kv_offload_cpu_cache_usage_perc{model_name="model",engine="0"} 0.75
+            vllm:kv_offload_load_bytes_total{model_name="model",engine="0"} 8192.0
+            vllm:kv_offload_size_count{model_name="model",engine="0",transfer_type="GPU_to_CPU"} 4
+            vllm:kv_offload_size_sum{model_name="model",engine="0",transfer_type="GPU_to_CPU"} 10000000.0
+            vllm:kv_offload_store_size_count{model_name="model",engine="0"} 4
+            vllm:kv_offload_store_size_sum{model_name="model",engine="0"} 10000000.0
+            vllm:kv_offload_store_time_total{model_name="model",engine="0"} 0.5
+            vllm:kv_offload_tiering_chunk_hits_total{model_name="model",engine="0",tier="1:kvcr"} 6.0
+            vllm:kv_offload_tiering_promotion_latency_seconds_count{model_name="model",engine="0",tier="1:kvcr",result="success"} 2

+            vllm:kv_offload_total_time_total{model_name="model",engine="0",transfer_type="GPU_to_CPU"} 0.5"#]].assert_eq(&kv_offload_series());
+    }

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""ShardQ split of the ROCm FP8 sparse-indexer prefill (DeepSeek-V4.1).
+
+One GPU plays every TP rank: each rank scores its zigzag tokens, which must
+select what the replicated run selects for them, including a candidate
+consumer whose candidate rows of other ranks hold junk; the exchange then puts
+every row back in token order. Rows compare as sets: the top-k order within a
+row depends on the batch shape."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform

+def run_dp_sharded_hyv4_vision_tower(
+    visual: HYV4VisionTransformer,
+    pixel_values: torch.Tensor,
+    grid_thw: list[list[int]],
+    modality: str,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+    """Run the HYV4 vision tower with whole media items sharded across the
+    TP group (`--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`).
+
+    Every rank holds the full tower weights and receives the full batch.
+    Items are assigned to ranks by patch count, each rank encodes only its
+    share, and per-item embeddings are exchanged with one padded all-gather
+    and returned in the original item order on every rank.
+
+    Unlike `run_dp_sharded_mrope_vision_model`, per-item output rows come
+    from `vision_token_count`: the merger adds newline/extra tokens and
+    pools video frames, so rows differ from `prod(grid) // merge**2`.
+    """
+    tp_size = get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+    tp_rank = get_tensor_model_parallel_rank()
+
+    patches_per_item = [t * h * w for t, h, w in grid_thw]
+    cum_patches = [0, *itertools.accumulate(patches_per_item)]
+    (item_to_rank, items_per_rank, _) = get_load_balance_assignment(
+        patches_per_item, tp_size
+    )
+    cum_items_per_rank = [0, *itertools.accumulate(items_per_rank)]
+
+    def rank_items(rank: int) -> list[int]:
+        return item_to_rank[cum_items_per_rank[rank] : cum_items_per_rank[rank + 1]]
+
+    # All-gather needs one shape on every rank; pad each rank's packed
+    # output to the largest per-rank row count (computable locally).
+    rows_per_item = [
+        vision_token_count(grid, visual.config, modality) for grid in grid_thw
+    ]
+    max_rows = max(sum(rows_per_item[i] for i in rank_items(r)) for r in range(tp_size))
+
+    local_items = rank_items(tp_rank)
+    if local_items:
+        pixels_local = torch.cat(
+            [pixel_values[cum_patches[i] : cum_patches[i + 1]] for i in local_items]
+        )
+        embeds_local = torch.cat(
+            visual(pixels_local, [grid_thw[i] for i in local_items]), dim=0
+        )
+    else:
+        # Empty ranks all-gather placeholders in the tower's parameter dtype
+        # (`visual.dtype`, the patch-embedding weight dtype for HYV4). HY4's
+        # tower is homogeneous-dtype, so this is also its output dtype; a
+        # tower with split dtypes would need its merger's weight dtype here
+        # instead (cf. DeepSeek-VL's aligner.w2.weight.dtype).
+        embeds_local = torch.empty(
+            (0, visual.config.out_hidden_size),
+            device=visual.device,
+            dtype=visual.dtype,
+        )
+    if embeds_local.shape[0] < max_rows:
+        embeds_local = torch.cat(
+            (
+                embeds_local,
+                embeds_local.new_empty(
+                    (max_rows - embeds_local.shape[0], embeds_local.shape[1])
+                ),
+            ),
+            dim=0,
+        )
+
+    gathered = tensor_model_parallel_all_gather(embeds_local.contiguous(), dim=0)
+
+    out: list[torch.Tensor | None] = [None] * len(grid_thw)
+    for rank in range(tp_size):
+        offset = rank * max_rows
+        for i in rank_items(rank):
+            out[i] = gathered[offset : offset + rows_per_item[i]]
+            offset += rows_per_item[i]
+    assert all(embed is not None for embed in out), "Found unassigned embeddings"
+    return tuple(out)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Host-side PLE row staging for NVIDIA Qwen4Exp.
+
+When unified virtual addressing (UVA) is unavailable, CPU offload gathers the
+requested rows from host RAM and copies them to the GPU before each forward.
+Disk offload uses the same staging buffers for rows read from checkpoint files.
+"""
+
+from abc import abstractmethod
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.gpu_sync_debug import gpu_sync_allowed
+
+from ..common.ngram_embedding import (
+    Qwen4ExpPLEEmbedding,
+    Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod,
+    Qwen4ExpPLENvFp4EmbeddingMethod,
+)
+
+
+class Qwen4ExpPLEHostStagedEmbedding(Qwen4ExpPLEEmbedding):
+    """Stage host rows outside the forward into fixed CUDA graph inputs."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        num_embeddings: int,
+        embedding_dim: int,
+        *,
+        params_dtype: torch.dtype,
+        padding_size: int,
+        prefix: str,
+        embedding_method: Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod,
+        num_ngram_heads: int = 1,
+        max_total_tokens: int = 0,
+        data_parallel_rank: int = 0,
+        reduce_results: bool = True,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(
+            num_embeddings,
+            embedding_dim,
+            params_dtype=params_dtype,
+            padding_size=padding_size,
+            prefix=prefix,
+            embedding_method=embedding_method,
+            data_parallel_rank=data_parallel_rank,
+            reduce_results=reduce_results,
+        )
+        # NVFP4 rows are packed E2M1 bytes plus a separate plane of block scales.
+        self._nvfp4 = isinstance(embedding_method, Qwen4ExpPLENvFp4EmbeddingMethod)
+        device = torch.get_default_device()
+        self._pin_memory = (
+            device.type == "cuda" and current_platform.is_pin_memory_available()
+        )
+        rows = (max_total_tokens, num_ngram_heads)
+        self._host_ids = torch.empty(
+            rows, dtype=torch.long, device="cpu", pin_memory=self._pin_memory
+        )
+        # The step sync completes the previous H2D before we reuse these buffers.
+        self._planes: dict[str, tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = {}
+        for name in ("weight", "weight_scale") if self._nvfp4 else ("weight",):
+            plane = getattr(self, name)
+            shape, dtype = (*rows, plane.shape[1]), plane.dtype
+            host = torch.empty(
+                shape, dtype=dtype, device="cpu", pin_memory=self._pin_memory
+            )
+            self._planes[name] = (
+                torch.zeros(shape, dtype=dtype, device=device),
+                host,
+            )
+        if self._nvfp4:
+            self._output = torch.zeros(
+                (*rows, embedding_dim), dtype=params_dtype, device=device
+            )
+            self._row_ids = torch.arange(rows[0] * rows[1], device=device)
+
+    def _copy(self, dst: torch.Tensor, src: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        if self._pin_memory:
+            dst.copy_(src, non_blocking=True)
+        else:
+            # Pageable host buffers require a synchronous transfer.
+            with gpu_sync_allowed():
+                dst.copy_(src)
+
+    def copy_ids_to_host(self, ids: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        self._copy(self._host_ids[: ids.shape[0]], ids)
+
+    def stage_rows(self, num_tokens: int) -> None:
+        self._gather_host_rows(self._host_ids[:num_tokens])
+        for staging, host in self._planes.values():
+            self._copy(staging[:num_tokens], host[:num_tokens])
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def _gather_host_rows(self, ids: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        """Fill the host buffers in the token and head order of `ids`."""
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    def staged_rows(self, num_tokens: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Return this step's staged rows, decoded if they are NVFP4."""
+        weight, *scale = (staging[:num_tokens] for staging, _ in self._planes.values())
+        if not self._nvfp4:
+            return weight.flatten(-2)
+        num_rows = weight.shape[0] * weight.shape[1]
+        output = self._output[:num_tokens]
+        # Staged rows are compact, so the i-th staged row has id i.
+        Qwen4ExpPLENvFp4EmbeddingMethod.decode_rows(
+            weight,
+            scale[0],
+            self.weight_scale_2,
+            self._row_ids[:num_rows],
+            output,
+            0,
+            num_rows,
+        )
+        return output.flatten(-2)
+
+    def start_prefetch(self, ngram_ids: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        return None
+
+    def finalize_prefetch(self, total_tokens: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        raise RuntimeError("Host-staged PLE embedding does not support prefetch")
+
+
+class Qwen4ExpPLEHostMemoryEmbedding(Qwen4ExpPLEHostStagedEmbedding):
+    """Gather this rank's CPU-resident PLE rows when UVA is unavailable."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+        if self.etp_data_parallel_size != 1:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "Host-memory PLE embedding does not support ETP spanning DP ranks"
+            )
+
+    def allocate_embedding_weight(
+        self,
+        num_embeddings: int,
+        embedding_dim: int,
+        dtype: torch.dtype,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Allocate the local ETP rows in ordinary CPU memory."""
+        return torch.empty(num_embeddings, embedding_dim, dtype=dtype, device="cpu")
+
+    def _gather_host_rows(self, ids: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        num_tokens = ids.shape[0]
+        ids = ids.flatten()
+        unowned = None
+        if self.tp_size > 1:
+            if ((ids < 0) | (ids >= self.org_vocab_size)).any():
+                raise IndexError(f"PLE id out of range for {self.org_vocab_size} rows")
+            start = self.shard_indices.org_vocab_start_index
+            end = self.shard_indices.org_vocab_end_index
+            unowned = (ids < start) | (ids >= end)
+            ids = (ids - start).masked_fill_(unowned, 0)
+
+        for name, (_, host) in self._planes.items():
+            table = getattr(self, name).view(torch.uint8)
+            out = host[:num_tokens].flatten(0, 1).view(torch.uint8)
+            torch.index_select(table, 0, ids, out=out)
+            if unowned is not None:
+                out[unowned] = 0
+
+    def staged_rows(self, num_tokens: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Return the staged rows combined across ETP ranks."""
+        embeddings = super().staged_rows(num_tokens)
+        if self.reduce_results:
+            return self._reduce_etp_embeddings(embeddings)
+        return embeddings

+def _uses_gemm(fn) -> bool:
+    """Whether `fn` took the dense GEMM path rather than BGMV."""
+    with torch.profiler.profile(
+        activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU]
+    ) as prof:
+        fn()
+    names = {event.name for event in prof.events()}
+    return bool(names & {"aten::mm", "aten::addmm"})
+
+
+def _lora_linear_reference(
+    y, x, lora_a, lora_b, indices, output_slices, scaling, add_inputs
+):
+    expected = y.float().clone()
+    offset = 0
+    for a, b, n in zip(lora_a, lora_b, output_slices):
+        for token, slot in enumerate(indices.tolist()):
+            if slot < 0:
+                # BGMV leaves rows without an adapter untouched.
+                continue
+            hidden = (x[token].float() @ a[slot, 0].float().t() * scaling).to(x.dtype)
+            delta = hidden.float() @ b[slot, 0].float().t()
+            if add_inputs:
+                expected[token, offset : offset + n] += delta
+            else:
+                expected[token, offset : offset + n] = delta
+        offset += n
+    return expected.to(y.dtype)
+
+
+def _make_lora_weights(output_slices, num_loras, rank, hidden_size, dtype, device):
+    lora_a = [
+        torch.randn(num_loras, 1, rank, hidden_size, dtype=dtype, device=device) * 0.1
+        for _ in output_slices
+    ]
+    lora_b = [
+        torch.randn(num_loras, 1, n, rank, dtype=dtype, device=device) * 0.1
+        for n in output_slices
+    ]
+    return lora_a, lora_b
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mapping", ["single", "mixed", "with_base", "small"])

+    device, rank, hidden_size, scaling = "xpu:0", 16, 512, 0.5
+    output_slices = [384, 128, 128]
+    num_tokens = 8 if mapping == "small" else 256
+    lora_a, lora_b = _make_lora_weights(
+        output_slices, 3, rank, hidden_size, dtype, device
+    )
+    indices = torch.full((num_tokens,), 1, dtype=torch.long)
+    if mapping == "mixed":
+        indices[num_tokens // 2 :] = 2
+    elif mapping == "with_base":
+        indices[num_tokens // 2 :] = -1
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, hidden_size, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    y = torch.randn(num_tokens, sum(output_slices), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    expected = _lora_linear_reference(
+        y, x, lora_a, lora_b, indices, output_slices, scaling, add_inputs
+    )
+
+    # The wrapper only reports a single slot when every token uses it.
+    slot = 1 if mapping in ("single", "small") else -1
+    single_lora_slot = torch.full((1,), slot, dtype=torch.int32)
+    used_gemm = _uses_gemm(
+        lambda: lora_linear(
+            y,
+            x,
+            lora_a,
+            lora_b,
+            indices.to(device),
+            single_lora_slot,
+            output_slices,
+            scaling,
+            add_inputs,
+            True,
+            64,

+    )
+    assert used_gemm == (mapping == "single")
+    assert_close(y, expected)
+
+

+        ("FULL_AND_PIECEWISE", 1024, "single", 600, False),

+    # Adapter ids 2 and 3 occupy slots 0 and 1; id 0 means no adapter.
+    token_ids = [3] * num_tokens
+    if mapping == "mixed":
+        token_ids[num_tokens // 2 :] = [2] * (num_tokens - num_tokens // 2)
+    elif mapping == "with_base":
+        token_ids[num_tokens // 2 :] = [0] * (num_tokens - num_tokens // 2)
+    wrapper.update_metadata(
+        LoRAMapping(tuple(token_ids), tuple(token_ids)), [2, 3], 2, 32000
+    )
+    # The slot is only recorded when the batch can take the GEMM path.
+    can_gemm = cudagraph_mode is not None and num_tokens > max_capture
+    expect_slot = 1 if mapping == "single" and can_gemm else -1
+    assert int(wrapper._single_lora_slot[0]) == expect_slot
+    slot_of = {0: -1, 2: 0, 3: 1}
+    indices = torch.tensor([slot_of[i] for i in token_ids])
+
+    lora_a, lora_b = _make_lora_weights(
+        output_slices, 2, rank, hidden_size, dtype, device
+    )
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, hidden_size, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    y = torch.randn(num_tokens, sum(output_slices), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+    expected = _lora_linear_reference(
+        y, x, lora_a, lora_b, indices, output_slices, 1.0, True

+    used_gemm = _uses_gemm(
+        lambda: wrapper.add_lora_linear(
+            y, x, tuple(lora_a), tuple(lora_b), 1.0, output_slices
+        )
+    )
+    assert used_gemm == expect_gemm
+    assert_close(y, expected)

+    "architectures": ["MuseSparkDSparkModel"],

+def _checkpoint_tensors() -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    """The tensor names and shapes of the Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark checkpoint."""
+    q, kv, ffn = HEADS * HEAD_DIM, KV_HEADS * HEAD_DIM, 2 * HIDDEN
+    shapes = {
+        "fc.weight": (HIDDEN, TINY_TEXT["hidden_size"] * len(DSPARK_TARGETS)),
+        "hidden_norm.weight": (HIDDEN,),
+        "norm.weight": (HIDDEN,),
+        "lm_head.weight": (VOCAB, HIDDEN),
+        "markov_head.markov_w1.weight": (VOCAB, RANK),
+        "markov_head.markov_w2.weight": (VOCAB, RANK),
+        "confidence_head.proj.weight": (1, HIDDEN + RANK),
+        "confidence_head.proj.bias": (1,),
+    }
+    for i in range(2):
+        layer = f"layers.{i}"
+        shapes |= {
+            f"{layer}.add_attn.gate": (HIDDEN,),
+            f"{layer}.add_ffn.gate": (HIDDEN,),
+            f"{layer}.pre_ffn_norm.weight": (HIDDEN,),
+            f"{layer}.post_ffn_norm.weight": (HIDDEN,),
+            f"{layer}.self_attn.pre_qkv_proj_norm.weight": (HIDDEN,),
+            f"{layer}.self_attn.q_proj.weight": (q, HIDDEN),
+            f"{layer}.self_attn.k_proj.weight": (kv, HIDDEN),
+            f"{layer}.self_attn.v_proj.weight": (kv, HIDDEN),
+            f"{layer}.self_attn.o_gate_proj.weight": (q, HIDDEN),
+            f"{layer}.self_attn.o_proj.weight": (HIDDEN, q),
+            f"{layer}.feed_forward.gate_proj.weight": (ffn, HIDDEN),
+            f"{layer}.feed_forward.up_proj.weight": (ffn, HIDDEN),
+            f"{layer}.feed_forward.down_proj.weight": (HIDDEN, ffn),
+        }
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    tensors = {
+        name: (torch.randn(shape, generator=gen) * 0.05).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        for name, shape in shapes.items()
+    }
+    tensors["d2t"] = torch.zeros(VOCAB, dtype=torch.long)
+    return tensors
+

+            method="dspark",
+            num_speculative_tokens=7,
+            attention_backend="ROCM_AITER_FA",
+            target_model_config=model_config,
+            target_parallel_config=parallel_config,
+            **spec,
+        ),
+        cache_config=CacheConfig(block_size=16),
+        attention_config=AttentionConfig(backend="ROCM_AITER_FA"),

+def _load_draft(checkpoints, **spec):
+    """The draft as `load_dspark_model` builds and loads it."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.model_loader import get_model
+    from vllm.model_executor.models.utils import get_draft_quant_config
+
+    vllm_config = _vllm_config(checkpoints, **spec)
+    vllm_config.quant_config = get_draft_quant_config(vllm_config)
+    draft_model_config = vllm_config.speculative_config.draft_model_config
+    with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
+        return get_model(vllm_config=vllm_config, model_config=draft_model_config)
+
+
+def _fp8_per_channel(w: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """BF16 dequantization of the online `fp8_per_channel` weight of `w`."""
+    fp8_max = torch.tensor(torch.finfo(F8).max, dtype=torch.float32, device=w.device)
+    scale = (w.abs().amax(-1).float() / fp8_max).clamp_min(1.0 / (fp8_max * 512))
+    q = (w.float() / scale[:, None]).clamp(-fp8_max, fp8_max).to(F8)
+    return (q.float() * scale[:, None]).bfloat16()
+
+
+def _rel(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    return ((a.float() - b.float()).norm() / b.float().norm()).item()

+## 4  Encoder cache events
+
+Encoder cache (EC) events mirror [KV cache events](kv_offloading_usage.md) so a
+router or cache-aware orchestrator can tell which instances already hold the
+encoder output for a given multimodal input. Events are keyed by the multimodal
+hash (`mm_hash`) and use the same ZMQ publisher and replay buffer as KV events.
+
+Enable them on the scheduler with `--ec-events-config`:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <model> \
+  --ec-events-config '{"enable_ec_cache_events": true, "publisher": "zmq", "topic": "ec-events"}'
+```
+
+The default endpoint is `tcp://*:6558`. Like KV events, the port is shifted up
+by the data-parallel rank; the block starts 1000 ports above the 5557/5558 KV
+events block, so both streams can be enabled at once on hosts with up to 1000
+DP ranks without an explicit `endpoint`.
+
+The event types are `ECStored(mm_hashes, medium)`, `ECRemoved(mm_hashes,
+medium)` and `AllECCleared()`, delivered in an `ECEventBatch`. The GPUs of the
+scheduler's own encoder cache report `medium="GPU"`; a connector that offloads
+encoder outputs adds its own events through `ECConnectorBase.take_events()`.
+Local GPU cache events are published even when no EC connector is configured.
+
+Events are off by default and use the `null` publisher when disabled. Subscribe
+the same way as for KV events, decoding `ECEventBatch` from
+`vllm.distributed.ec_transfer.ec_events`; see
+[kv_events_subscriber.py](../../examples/features/kv_events/kv_events_subscriber.py)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Encoder cache (EC) events.
+
+Mirror the KV cache events in `vllm.distributed.kv_events` so routers and
+cache-aware orchestrators can track which instances hold encoder outputs for
+which multimodal inputs. Events are keyed by `mm_hash` instead of block hash.
+"""
+
+import msgspec
+
+from vllm.distributed.kv_events import EventBatch
+
+
+class ECCacheEvent(
+    msgspec.Struct,
+    omit_defaults=True,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    gc=False,  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+    tag=True,
+):
+    """Base class for all encoder cache-related events."""
+
+
+class ECStored(ECCacheEvent):
+    mm_hashes: list[str]
+    medium: str | None
+
+
+class ECRemoved(ECCacheEvent):
+    mm_hashes: list[str]
+    medium: str | None
+
+
+class AllECCleared(ECCacheEvent):
+    pass
+
+
+class ECEventBatch(EventBatch):
+    events: list[ECStored | ECRemoved | AllECCleared]

+class PPMicrobatchCap:
+    """Caps each PP step's token budget at the uncached prefill backlog /
+    pp_size (at least `min_tokens`) plus running decode tokens, so a light
+    prefill load is split into chunks that fill every pipeline stage."""
+
+    def __init__(self, scheduler: "Scheduler", pp_size: int, min_tokens: int):
+        self.scheduler = scheduler
+        self.pp_size = pp_size
+        self.min_tokens = min_tokens
+        # (num_tokens, prefix-cache hit, probed cached prefix) of waiting requests.
+        self._cached_tokens = weakref.WeakKeyDictionary[Request, tuple[int, int, int]]()
+
+    @classmethod
+    def create(cls, scheduler: "Scheduler", pp_size: int) -> "PPMicrobatchCap | None":
+        """None without PP, when disabled, or when prefills can't be freely
+        chunked."""
+        config = scheduler.scheduler_config
+        if (
+            pp_size == 1
+            or not config.pp_microbatch_min_tokens
+            or not config.enable_chunked_prefill
+            or config.disable_chunked_mm_input
+            or scheduler.need_mamba_block_aligned_split
+        ):
+            return None
+        return cls(scheduler, pp_size, config.pp_microbatch_min_tokens)
+
+    def apply(self, budget: int) -> int:
+        scheduler = self.scheduler
+        waiting_queues = (
+            scheduler.kv_holding_waiting,
+            scheduler.waiting,
+            scheduler.async_kv_waiting,
+        )
+        # Parked async KV loads are counted with the waiting requests.
+        prefill = sum(
+            max(0, request.num_tokens - request.num_computed_tokens)
+            for request in scheduler._inflight_prefills
+            if request.status == RequestStatus.RUNNING
+        )
+        if not prefill and not any(waiting_queues):
+            return budget  # No prefill to split.
+        decode = sum(
+            1 + len(request.spec_token_ids)
+            for request in scheduler.running
+            if request.num_computed_tokens >= request.num_prompt_tokens
+            and not scheduler._needs_no_more_steps(request)
+        )
+        for request in itertools.chain(*waiting_queues):
+            if prefill >= budget * self.pp_size:
+                break  # cap already at the full budget
+            hit = self._num_cached_tokens(request)
+            prefill += max(0, request.num_tokens - hit)
+        # num_prefill_lookahead: the MTP lookahead reservation must leave a token.
+        cap = max(
+            self.min_tokens,
+            scheduler.num_prefill_lookahead,
+            cdiv(prefill, self.pp_size),
+        )
+        return min(budget, cap + decode)
+
+    def _num_cached_tokens(self, request: Request) -> int:
+        """`get_num_cached_tokens`, redone only when num_tokens changes
+        (preemption) or more of the request's prefix has been cached since."""
+        kv_cache_manager = self.scheduler.kv_cache_manager
+        cached = self._cached_tokens.get(request)
+        if cached is not None and cached[0] == request.num_tokens:
+            _, num_cached, prefix = cached
+            if kv_cache_manager.extend_cached_prefix(request, prefix) == prefix:
+                return num_cached
+        num_cached = kv_cache_manager.get_num_cached_tokens(request)
+        prefix = kv_cache_manager.extend_cached_prefix(request, num_cached)
+        self._cached_tokens[request] = (request.num_tokens, num_cached, prefix)
+        return num_cached

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Workload snapshots that accompany iteration records.
+
+All lengths are logical token counts, not physical KV cache occupancy.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.request import Request
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class ScheduledWorkload:
+    """KV context lengths of the requests scheduled in one iteration.
+
+    A request's context is what it has computed before the iteration. Its
+    prefill length is that context plus half of the tokens scheduled for it,
+    about the mean context of those tokens. The variances are population
+    variances. The request and token counts are in the iteration's record,
+    where prefill is `num_ctx_*` and decode is `num_generation_*`. With async
+    scheduling and speculative decoding, a decode context can exceed the true
+    one by the draft tokens that the previous, still running iteration rejects.
+    """
+
+    sum_prefill_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class QueuedWorkload:
+    """Requests in the waiting queues when the scheduler stats were made,
+    deferred ones included. Stats are made on engine steps, so an idle engine
+    does not update it.
+
+    Preempted requests and requests waiting for remote KV count as queued
+    decode work with their computed tokens, which a preemption resets to zero
+    and an admitted remote load sets before the KV arrives. The other requests,
+    streaming sessions that wait for more input included, count as queued
+    prefill work with all their tokens. This is a queue category, not an
+    execution phase: a resumed request may have to recompute its prefill.
+    """
+
+    num_prefill_requests: int = 0
+    sum_prefill_tokens: int = 0
+    var_prefill_length: float = 0.0
+    num_decode_requests: int = 0
+    sum_decode_kv_tokens: int = 0
+    var_decode_kv_tokens: float = 0.0
+
+
+def _variance(count: int, total: int, total_squares: int) -> float:
+    """Population variance, exact up to the final division."""
+    if not count:
+        return 0.0
+    return (count * total_squares - total * total) / (count * count)
+
+
+def _variance_of(lengths: list[int]) -> float:
+    return _variance(len(lengths), sum(lengths), sum(x * x for x in lengths))
+
+
+def make_scheduled_workload(
+    new_requests: Iterable["Request"],
+    running_requests: Iterable["Request"],
+    num_scheduled_tokens: Mapping[str, int],
+) -> ScheduledWorkload:
+    """Summarize the scheduled requests before their computed tokens advance.
+
+    Prefill and decode requests are told apart as in `IterationDetails`.
+    """
+    prefill_kv_tokens = 0
+    # Twice the prefill length, to keep half tokens exact.
+    prefill_lengths: list[int] = []
+    decode_lengths: list[int] = []
+    for requests, is_new in ((new_requests, True), (running_requests, False)):
+        for request in requests:
+            kv_tokens = request.num_computed_tokens
+            if is_new or request.is_prefill_chunk:
+                prefill_kv_tokens += kv_tokens
+                prefill_lengths.append(
+                    2 * kv_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens[request.request_id]
+                )
+            else:
+                decode_lengths.append(kv_tokens)
+    return ScheduledWorkload(
+        sum_prefill_kv_tokens=prefill_kv_tokens,
+        var_prefill_length=_variance_of(prefill_lengths) / 4,
+        sum_decode_kv_tokens=sum(decode_lengths),
+        var_decode_kv_tokens=_variance_of(decode_lengths),
+    )
+
+
+class QueuedWorkloadTally:
+    """The `QueuedWorkload` of the waiting queues, kept as requests enter and
+    leave them.
+
+    A request is remembered as it was counted, so that leaving subtracts
+    exactly that. One whose status or token counts change while it waits must
+    be passed to `refresh`.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        # vllm.v1.request imports this module through vllm.v1.metrics.stats.
+        from vllm.v1.request import RequestStatus
+
+        self._decode_statuses = (
+            RequestStatus.PREEMPTED,
+            RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS,
+        )
+        # request -> (its queue, whether it is decode work, its length)
+        self._counted: dict[Request, tuple[object, bool, int]] = {}
+        # [count, sum, sum of squares] of the prefill and of the decode lengths.
+        self._totals: tuple[list[int], list[int]] = ([0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0])
+
+    def add(self, queue: object, request: "Request") -> None:
+        """Count a request that entered `queue`, as it is now."""
+        counted = self._counted.get(request)
+        if counted is not None:
+            self.discard(counted[0], request)
+        is_decode = request.status in self._decode_statuses
+        length = request.num_computed_tokens if is_decode else request.num_tokens
+        self._counted[request] = (queue, is_decode, length)
+        totals = self._totals[is_decode]
+        totals[0] += 1
+        totals[1] += length
+        totals[2] += length * length
+
+    def discard(self, queue: object, request: "Request") -> None:
+        """Stop counting a request that left `queue`, if it was in it."""
+        counted = self._counted.get(request)
+        if counted is not None and counted[0] is queue:
+            del self._counted[request]
+            _, is_decode, length = counted
+            totals = self._totals[is_decode]
+            totals[0] -= 1
+            totals[1] -= length
+            totals[2] -= length * length
+
+    def refresh(self, request: "Request") -> None:
+        """Recount a waiting request that changed in place."""
+        counted = self._counted.get(request)
+        if counted is not None:
+            self.add(counted[0], request)
+
+    def summary(self) -> QueuedWorkload:
+        prefill, decode = self._totals
+        return QueuedWorkload(
+            num_prefill_requests=prefill[0],
+            sum_prefill_tokens=prefill[1],
+            var_prefill_length=_variance(*prefill),
+            num_decode_requests=decode[0],
+            sum_decode_kv_tokens=decode[1],
+            var_decode_kv_tokens=_variance(*decode),
+        )

    The two halves are published together or not at all. An `mm_hash` the producer cannot serve — never saved because the region was full, or evicted since — is reported with empty `metadata` and no address, so an orchestrator leaves the media on the request and the consumer encodes it locally.
 2. The orchestrator issues a follow-up request with the same `mm_hash` to a consumer instance, passing the producer's `ec_transfer_params` through `SamplingParams.extra_args["ec_transfer_params"]`.
-3. On the consumer, `ECCPUScheduler.ensure_cache_available()` reads `request.ec_transfer_params`. For each `mm_hash` not already cached locally, it opens a ZMQ session to `(peer_host, peer_port)`, sends an `XferReq`, and on an `OK` `XferAck` issues a NIXL READ that pulls the blocks straight from the producer's mmap into its own. The request is deferred until the READ completes.
+3. On the consumer, `ECCPUScheduler.ensure_cache_available()` checks `request.ec_transfer_params`. A ready CPU-tier entry or a runner encoder-cache entry with a matching embedding count avoids a remote transfer. For each announced `mm_hash` without either cache hit, it opens a ZMQ session to `(peer_host, peer_port)`, sends an `XferReq`, and on an `OK` `XferAck` issues a NIXL READ that pulls the blocks straight from the producer's mmap into its own. The request is deferred until the READ completes.
 4. A `NACK_NOT_READY` means the producer announced the encoding but its GPU→mmap save has not landed yet. The consumer releases the in-flight entry without recording a failure and re-requests the read on a later step, so a save that lands a few steps late costs latency rather than a recompute.
 5. On any other NACK (`NACK_MISSING`, `NACK_INCOMPAT`, `NACK_VERSION`, `NACK_INTERNAL`), ack timeout, read timeout, or peer disconnect, the consumer discards the in-flight entry and falls back to local encoding for that `mm_hash` — a P2P failure never blocks the request indefinitely.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Fused GDN prefill causal conv1d + post-conv prep (csrc/mamba/gdn_prefill_conv.cu).
+
+Covers bf16, head dim 128, width-4 conv without bias, and SiLU; callers fall
+back to `causal_conv1d_fn` + `fused_post_conv_prep` otherwise.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm._custom_ops import gdn_prefill_conv as _gdn_conv_cpp
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import NULL_BLOCK_ID
+
+_STATE_LEN = 3  # width-4 taps
+
+
+def gdn_prefill_conv_supported(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_states: torch.Tensor,
+    head_k_dim: int,
+    head_v_dim: int,
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether the kernel covers these tensors. Bias and activation are checked
+    by the caller."""
+    return (
+        current_platform.is_cuda()
+        # older precompiled extensions may lack the op
+        and hasattr(torch.ops._C, "gdn_prefill_conv")
+        and x.is_cuda
+        and x.dim() == 2
+        and x.stride(1) == 1
+        and x.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and conv_states.dtype == x.dtype
+        and weight.dtype == x.dtype
+        and weight.dim() == 2
+        and weight.size(0) == x.size(1)
+        and weight.size(1) == _STATE_LEN + 1
+        and conv_states.dim() == 3
+        and conv_states.size(1) == x.size(1)
+        and conv_states.size(2) >= _STATE_LEN
+        and head_k_dim == head_v_dim == 128
+        and x.size(1) % head_k_dim == 0
+        and weight.stride(1) == 1
+        and weight.stride(0) == 4
+        and (x.stride(0) * x.element_size()) % 8 == 0
+        and x.data_ptr() % 8 == 0  # vectorized 8B loads
+    )
+
+
+def gdn_prefill_conv(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_states: torch.Tensor,
+    query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
+    cache_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    has_initial_state: torch.Tensor,
+    a: torch.Tensor,
+    b: torch.Tensor,
+    A_log: torch.Tensor,
+    dt_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    num_k_heads: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+    output_g_exp: bool = False,
+    beta_scale: float = 1.0,
+    null_block_id: int | None = NULL_BLOCK_ID,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """SiLU causal conv of `x` (tokens, [Q | K | V]), then the post-conv prep.
+
+    Updates `conv_states` in place. Returns q, k (tokens, H, D), v
+    (tokens, HV, D), and fp32 g, beta (tokens, HV).
+    """
+    num_tokens = x.size(0)
+    H, HV, D = num_k_heads, A_log.size(0), head_dim
+    assert x.size(1) == (2 * H + HV) * D
+    assert A_log.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert dt_bias.dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float32)
+    q = torch.empty(num_tokens, H, D, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+    k = torch.empty(num_tokens, H, D, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+    v = torch.empty(num_tokens, HV, D, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+    g = torch.empty(num_tokens, HV, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+    beta = torch.empty(num_tokens, HV, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+    num_seqs = query_start_loc.size(0) - 1
+    if num_tokens == 0 or num_seqs == 0:
+        return q, k, v, g, beta
+    _gdn_conv_cpp(
+        x,
+        weight,
+        conv_states,
+        query_start_loc,
+        cache_indices,
+        has_initial_state,
+        a,
+        b,
+        A_log,
+        dt_bias,
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        g,
+        beta,
+        num_k_heads,
+        head_dim,
+        output_g_exp,
+        beta_scale,
+        -1 if null_block_id is None else null_block_id,
+    )
+    return q, k, v, g, beta

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""SP (sequence-parallel) MoE half for large eager steps, TP4.
+
+Per MoE layer, rows padded to a multiple of TP, R = S_pad / TP rows a rank:
+
+1. reduce-scatter of the attention partial (AITER custom RS, else RCCL);
+2. fused add + Gemma RMSNorm (bf16 + MXFP8) of the rank's R rows with its
+   residual rows;
+3. router (the layer's GateLinear) and the shared expert (full replicated MXFP8
+   weights, AITER preshuffled GEMM) on the R rows;
+4. biased top-k (x routed scale) and MXFP4 quant of the R normed rows;
+5. all-gather of the FP4 codes and of (scales | ids | weights) (AITER custom AG,
+   else RCCL);
+6. the stock AITER A4W4 row for M = S on the gathered, prequantized rows
+   (aiter_moe.AiterMoe.run_prequant);
+7. shared output + the new residual rows added into the rank's own rows of the
+   routed partial, then one TP all-reduce.
+
+With the next layer's input norm (`_post_moe`), step 7 is a reduce-scatter of
+the routed partial instead, and the next layer gets its MXFP8 attention input
+(`Mxfp8Carry`). When the installed AITER has the fused MoE top-k combine +
+reduce-scatter (`fused_moe_combine_reduce_scatter`, ROCm/aiter#7771) and the
+stock row's stage 2 ends in the bf16 scatter epilogue (padded M >= 4096), the
+routed MoE stops before its top-k combine (`scatter_intermediate`) and that one
+launch does the combine and the reduce-scatter together: no [M, 6144] combined
+output, no padding copy. Otherwise the combine and the reduce-scatter run as
+before.
+
+The all-reduced result already holds the new residual, so the layer returns
+(result, zero residual): the next layer's fused add (or the final norm) adds a
+zero. The zero residual is a stride-0 view of one zero row (the fused-add Triton
+kernels take the residual's row stride)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+import inspect
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+from .carry import Mxfp8Carry
+from .shared import SharedWeights, shared_full
+
+TOPK_GROUPS = 4  # biased_grouped_topk(.., 4, 4, ..): every group kept, a flat top-k
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+HIDDEN, TOPK = 6144, 4
+FAULT_MESSAGE = (
+    "MiniMax-M3 SP: fused combine + reduce-scatter error record set (a peer wait "
+    "timed out)"
+)
+# Rows of a step the fused combine + reduce-scatter takes at most (its receive
+# buffer: 3 x ceil(rows / 4) x 12 KB a rank, 151 MB at 16384).
+SCATTER_RS_MAX_ROWS = 16384
+
+
+class SpPrefill:
+    def __init__(self, group, min_rows: int, max_rows: int) -> None:
+        self.group = group
+        self.rank = group.rank_in_group
+        self.world = group.world_size
+        self.min_rows = max(min_rows, self.world)
+        self.max_rows = max_rows
+        self._zero: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        # AITER's fused top-k combine + reduce-scatter buffers, once set up
+        self.combine_rs = None
+        self._err_view: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        self._capture = None  # tests: a dict that receives each run's top-k
+        self._setup_combine_rs()
+
+    def _setup_combine_rs(self) -> None:
+        """Collective, every TP rank at the same point (SpPrefill is built at
+        the first eager forward, vLLM's profile run, so the memory profile sees
+        the buffer). Off, with the old combine + reduce-scatter, when the
+        installed AITER lacks the op or the `scatter_intermediate` stage-2
+        keyword (ROCm/aiter#7771)."""
+        from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.common.peer_memory import tp_agree
+
+        cpu = self.group.cpu_group
+        ok, err = True, None
+        try:
+            if not aiter_combine_rs_available():
+                raise RuntimeError("AITER has no fused MoE combine + reduce-scatter")
+            from aiter.ops.triton.comms.fused.moe_combine_reduce_scatter import (
+                MoeCombineReduceScatter,
+            )
+        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
+            ok, err = False, e
+        if not tp_agree(ok, cpu):
+            logger.info(
+                "MiniMax-M3 SP: top-k combine + reduce-scatter unfused (%s)",
+                err or "refused on another rank",
+            )
+            return
+        comm: Any = None
+        try:
+            comm = MoeCombineReduceScatter(
+                cpu, SCATTER_RS_MAX_ROWS, HIDDEN, TOPK
+            )  # collective handshake
+        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
+            ok, err = False, e
+        if not tp_agree(ok, cpu):
+            logger.warning(
+                "MiniMax-M3 SP: fused combine + reduce-scatter setup failed on %s "
+                "rank: %s",
+                "this" if err else "another",
+                err,
+            )
+            if comm is not None:
+                comm.close()
+            return
+        self.combine_rs = comm
+        self._err_view = _error_record_view(comm)
+        if self.rank == 0:
+            logger.info(
+                "MiniMax-M3 SP: top-k combine fused into the post-MoE "
+                "reduce-scatter (AITER), up to %d rows, %.1f MB a rank",
+                SCATTER_RS_MAX_ROWS,
+                comm.nbytes / 1e6,
+            )
+
+    def assert_healthy(self) -> None:
+        """Device-side: traps the queue once a wait of the fused combine +
+        reduce-scatter timed out on any rank (its error record)."""
+        if self._err_view is not None:
+            torch._assert_async(self._err_view[0] == 0, FAULT_MESSAGE)
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        if self.combine_rs is not None:
+            self.combine_rs.close()
+            self.combine_rs = None
+            self._err_view = None
+
+    def zero_residual(self, rows: int, like: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if (
+            self._zero is None
+            or self._zero.shape[1] != like.shape[1]
+            or self._zero.dtype != like.dtype
+        ):
+            self._zero = torch.zeros(
+                1, like.shape[1], dtype=like.dtype, device=like.device
+            )
+        return self._zero.expand(rows, like.shape[1])
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------ collectives
+    def _aiter_comm(self):
+        ca = getattr(self.group.device_communicator, "aiter_ar_comm", None)
+        ca = getattr(ca, "_impl", ca)
+        return None if ca is None or getattr(ca, "disabled", True) else ca
+
+    def _reduce_scatter(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        from vllm.distributed import tensor_model_parallel_reduce_scatter
+
+        ca = self._aiter_comm()
+        if ca is not None and ca.should_custom_rs(x, 0):
+            out = torch.empty(
+                (x.shape[0] // self.world, x.shape[1]), dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device
+            )
+            ca.custom_reduce_scatter(x, out, dim=0)
+            return out
+        return tensor_model_parallel_reduce_scatter(x, dim=0)
+
+    def _all_gather(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Rows of a byte tensor from every rank, in rank order (bf16 carrier:
+        AITER's IPC gather takes 16/32-bit floats only)."""
+        from vllm.distributed import tensor_model_parallel_all_gather
+
+        x16 = x.contiguous().view(torch.bfloat16)
+        ca = self._aiter_comm()
+        if ca is not None and ca.should_custom_ag(x16):
+            return ca.custom_all_gather(x16, dim=0).view(torch.uint8)
+        return tensor_model_parallel_all_gather(x16, dim=0).view(torch.uint8)
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------ per layer
+    def run(
+        self,
+        layer,
+        part: torch.Tensor,
+        residual: torch.Tensor,
+        sw: SharedWeights,
+        aiter_moe,
+        nxt_norm=None,
+    ):
+        """`part`: this rank's unreduced o_proj output [S, H]; `residual`: [S, H], or
+        this rank's padded rows [R, H] (an Mxfp8Carry's). Without `nxt_norm`:
+        (all-reduced MoE output + new residual, zero residual). With the next layer's
+        input norm: the MoE partial reduce-scattered, + residual and shared rows, the
+        next layer's fused add + Gemma RMSNorm + MXFP8 quant on this rank's rows, the
+        codes and scales all-gathered -> (Mxfp8Carry, this rank's new residual rows)."""
+        import aiter
+        from aiter import dtypes
+        from aiter.ops.quant import per_1x32_mx_quant_hip
+
+        from vllm.distributed import tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce
+        from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.gemma_rmsnorm import (
+            gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8_and_bf16,
+        )
+
+        moe, norm = layer.block_sparse_moe, layer.post_attention_layernorm
+        s, h = part.shape
+        rows = -(-s // self.world)
+        if rows * self.world != s:
+            part = F.pad(part, (0, 0, 0, rows * self.world - s))
+        hs = self._reduce_scatter(part.contiguous())
+        lo = self.rank * rows
+        n = max(
+            0, min(rows, s - lo)
+        )  # this rank's real rows (the last may hold padding)
+        if (
+            residual.shape[0] == rows and s != rows
+        ):  # this rank's rows already (sharded residual)
+            res = residual
+        else:
+            res = residual[lo : lo + n]
+            if n < rows:
+                res = F.pad(res, (0, 0, 0, rows - n))
+        x_q, x_s, normed, res_new = gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8_and_bf16(
+            hs, res, norm.weight, norm.variance_epsilon
+        )
+        logits, _ = moe.gate(normed)
+        sh = shared_full(sw, moe.shared_experts, x_q, x_s)
+        topk = aiter_moe.topk
+        w = torch.empty((rows, topk), dtype=torch.float32, device=part.device)
+        ids = torch.empty((rows, topk), dtype=torch.int32, device=part.device)
+        aiter.biased_grouped_topk(
+            logits,
+            moe.e_score_correction_bias,
+            w,
+            ids,
+            TOPK_GROUPS,
+            TOPK_GROUPS,
+            True,
+            float(moe.routed_scaling_factor),
+        )
+        fp4, sc = per_1x32_mx_quant_hip(
+            normed, scale=None, quant_dtype=dtypes.fp4x2, shuffle=False
+        )
+        small = torch.cat(
+            [sc.view(torch.uint8), ids.view(torch.uint8), w.view(torch.uint8)], dim=1
+        )
+        fp4_all = self._all_gather(fp4.view(torch.uint8))  # [S_pad, H / 2]
+        small_all = self._all_gather(small)  # [S_pad, H / 32 + 8 topk]
+        g = h // 32
+        sc_all = small_all[:s, :g].contiguous()
+        ids_all = small_all[:s, g : g + 4 * topk].contiguous().view(torch.int32)
+        w_all = small_all[:s, g + 4 * topk :].contiguous().view(torch.float32)
+        if self._capture is not None:
+            self._capture.update(ids=ids_all, w=w_all)
+        # stage 2 stops before its top-k combine: the intermediate goes to the
+        # fused combine + reduce-scatter
+        defer = None
+        if (
+            nxt_norm is not None
+            and self.combine_rs is not None
+            and s <= SCATTER_RS_MAX_ROWS
+            and aiter_moe.scatter_deferrable(s)
+        ):
+            defer = {}
+        # routed partial, x routed scale (not written when `defer` comes back
+        # filled)
+        out = aiter_moe.run_prequant(fp4_all[:s], sc_all, ids_all, w_all, scatter=defer)
+        if nxt_norm is not None:
+            return self._post_moe(out, s, rows, res_new, sh, nxt_norm, defer)
+        if n:
+            mine = out[lo : lo + n]
+            mine += sh[:n]
+            mine += res_new[:n]
+        return tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(out), self.zero_residual(s, out)
+
+    def _post_moe(self, out, s, rows, res_new, sh, nxt_norm, defer=None):
+        """The MoE partial reduce-scattered (bf16), + this rank's residual and
+        shared rows, then the next layer's input norm with its MXFP8 quant on
+        these rows; codes and scales all-gathered (~0.52x a bf16 gather).
+        `defer` (filled by stage 2): the uncombined GEMM2 intermediate, whose
+        top-k combine then runs fused into the reduce-scatter."""
+        from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.gemma_rmsnorm import (
+            gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8,
+        )
+
+        if defer:
+            from aiter.ops.triton.comms.fused.moe_combine_reduce_scatter import (
+                fused_moe_combine_reduce_scatter,
+            )
+
+            # [R, H]: this rank's rows of the combined, reduce-scattered MoE
+            # output (x routed scale)
+            rs = fused_moe_combine_reduce_scatter(
+                defer["inter"],
+                defer["reverse_sorted"],
+                defer["sorted_weights"],
+                s,
+                self.combine_rs,
+            )
+        else:
+            if rows * self.world != s:
+                out = F.pad(out, (0, 0, 0, rows * self.world - s))
+            # [R, H]: this rank's rows of the MoE output
+            rs = self._reduce_scatter(out.contiguous())

+        x_q, x_s, res_out = gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8(
+            rs, res_in, nxt_norm.weight, nxt_norm.variance_epsilon

+    stage-2 `scatter_intermediate` keyword it consumes (ROCm/aiter#7771)."""

+        from aiter.ops.triton.comms.fused.moe_combine_reduce_scatter import (  # noqa: F401
+            MoeCombineReduceScatter,
+            fused_moe_combine_reduce_scatter,
+        )

+            "scatter_intermediate" in inspect.signature(getattr(fm, f)).parameters
+            for f in ("_flydsl_v2_stage2_wrapper", "_mxfp4_a4w4_stage2_fw")

+def _error_record_view(comm) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+    """A device view of the first word of `comm`'s error record (its own IPC
+    buffer starts with [flag, rank, colour, site]), for a check without a host

+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.common.peer_memory import _DeviceBytes
+

+    except (AttributeError, IndexError, TypeError, ValueError):
+        return None
+    view = torch.as_tensor(_DeviceBytes(base, 16), device=comm.device)
+    return view.view(torch.int32)

+    For synchronous media fetching, vLLM limits response-body streaming and
+    retries to twice the configured per-read timeout. This prevents a server
+    that continuously sends a few response-body bytes from occupying a
+    renderer worker indefinitely. The same limit applies to audio and video
+    URLs using `VLLM_AUDIO_FETCH_TIMEOUT` and `VLLM_VIDEO_FETCH_TIMEOUT`.
+    When a fetch exceeds this limit, the API returns HTTP 422 with `error.param`
+    set to the request field that supplied the URL.
+
 ### Video Inputs
 
 Instead of `image_url`, you can pass a video file via `video_url`. Here is a simple example using [LLaVA-OneVision](https://huggingface.co/llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf).
